input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Clause 3.4 is the only inspection/verification right binding the Company. It meets or beats the playbook on most material terms: 30 days' prior written notice (preferred), inspection limited to payment-calculation records during the Company's normal business hours, HDI bears all inspection costs unconditionally (better than the preferred 5% underpayment carve-out), and there is no right of access to Company systems. However, it contains no frequency limit at all, so the right could in principle be exercised repeatedly — failing both the preferred (once per 12 months) and the fallback (once per year) on a material term and approaching the walk-away position on unlimited audits. The redline inserts a once-per-twelve-month cap and changes nothing else. Two sub-elements short of preferred are noted but not flagged: the inspection is conducted by HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor, and confidentiality is not restated here (HDI's confidentiality obligations under clause 8.2 already cover Company Confidential Information).

proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per twelve-month period
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a once-per-twelve-month cap on HDI's inspection right, since as drafted the right could be exercised without limit. Notice, business-hours and cost-allocation terms are acceptable and are unchanged.

ops.oldText: may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records
ops.newText: may, not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records
